newsitem.title: USA: Lithuania plans to scrap currency board splits IMF.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania plans to scrap currency board splits IMF.

text.p: Lithuanian plans to scrap its currency board have prompted debate in the International Monetary Fund and the fund said on Monday some directors had questioned the logic of abandoning the scheme.

"A few (directors) considered that the medium-term exchange rate strategy announced by the Bank of Lithuania was appropriate, against a background of the authorities' desire to develop increased central bank functions," the IMF said in a statement released after a review of the Lithuanian economy.
"A few other directors, however, wondered about the wisdom of moving away from the currency board arrangement, which had served as a key element in achieving financial stabilization.
"They pointed out that the currency board arrangement had provided a credible monetary rule and that it could be adapted to deal with increasing financial sophistication."
A three-year Lithuanian currency program, announced early this year, envisages gradually replacing the currency board with a more traditional currency peg.
This would give the central bank more flexibility than with the current system, under which a rise in cash emission must be backed by higher reserves.

"Directors stressed the importance of ensuring a timely exit from the currency board arrangement, so as to maintain the confidence of market participants while safeguarding central bank independence and its lender of last resort function," the IMF said.
The litas is set at four to the dollar under the currency board.
